text.p: MICHIGAN, Aug 10 - New Zealand golfer Frank Nobilo has turned his thoughts to Thursday's United States PGA Championship after finishing 20th in the Buick Open in Michigan this morning (NZT).
NZPA reports Fiji's Vijay Singh earned his second tour win of the season when he stormed through the field on the final day with a six-under 66.

Singh won by four shots, at 15-under, ahead of six golfers tied for second at 11-under. Included in that group was overnight leader Ernie Els of South Africa and another dual US Open champion, Curtis Strange, who was recording his best finish
Singh, 34, pocketed $US270,000 ($NZ426,000) for his fifth PGA Tour win and took his winnings this season in America to well over $US825,000.

Singh has made a habit in recent years of winning Buick-sponsored tournaments and now adds a first Buick Open title to a pair of Buick Classic championship trophies he won in New York State in 1993 and 1995.
But the top of Singh's shopping list now is not another Buick title. He wants to win a major and he gets that chance starting on Thursday.
Els forfeited a three-shot third-round lead and was unable to rally against Singh's charge. He finished with a tired-looking two-over 74.
Nobilo, who paired with Tiger Woods for the final round, finished the tournament with rounds of 69, 71, 70 and 71 for a seven-under par total of 281.
"I showed patches of form but then showed enough rubbish as well that's given me plenty of work on," said Nobilo.
"Today I played good as well but just couldn't quite get on top of it."

Nobilo's round included three birdies and two bogeys while Woods, the player that Nobilo finished second to in the recent Western Open in Chicago, had five birdies and bogey in his round of 68 to go to 10-under and a share of eighth place.
Grant Waite's hope of a morale-boosting effort virtually evaporated within the first three holes of his last round.

The Palmerston North-born golfer, who began the day at six-under, bogeyed the par five first and then dropped a further shot at the par three third. However that was nothing compared to the face-slapping double-bogey six he took at the par four sixth.
He eventually finished with a three-over par 75, plummeting back into an overall share of 43rd place.
Waite, who is not eligible to contest the PGA Championship, is next entered to contest the Greater Vancouver Open beginning in a fortnight's time.
